gloss: botamochi; rice cake coated with sweet red bean paste

definitions.gloss: botamochi; sticky rice ball coated with sweet red bean paste
definitions.explanation: A traditional sweet made of pounded glutinous rice formed into a ball and covered with {あんこ|あんこ} (sweet red bean paste). It is closely associated with the spring equinox, when it is offered to ancestors.

examples.japanese: {牡丹餅|ぼたもち}を{作|つく}る。
お{彼岸|ひがん}に{牡丹餅|ぼたもち}を{供|そな}える。
examples.english: We offer botamochi at the equinox.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{春|はる}の{彼岸|ひがん}にいつも{牡丹餅|ぼたもち}を{作|つく}ってくれる。
examples.english: My grandmother always makes botamochi for the spring equinox.

notes:
Named after the {牡丹|ぼたん} (peony), a spring flower. The same sweet eaten at the autumn equinox is usually called おはぎ, named after the bush clover ({萩|はぎ}) that blooms then.

CULTURAL CONTEXT:
- Strongly tied to お{彼岸|ひがん} (the equinoxes), when it is offered at family altars and graves
- Source of the proverb {棚|たな}から{牡丹餅|ぼたもち} ("botamochi from a shelf"), meaning an unexpected stroke of luck
